audit.why: Zaahen taking levels 1-5 and the lane evening out into the group phase matches a 51.19% Sejuani win rate over 631 games — the largest sample in this champion's data. The kits agree: The Darkin Glaive is 10s at rank 1 and Aureate Rush 10s, against Arctic Assault's 18s and Winter's Wrath's 9s, so he gets roughly two full trade patterns for each of hers before items. The shape is right; the entry simply never says why in terms a player can act on.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's only flagged defect for this matchup is that there is no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in either layer, and it is correct: not one of Zaahen's five abilities is named. Both layers refer to 'his Q and E' and to 'Zaahen Ultimate', which is a placeholder rather than a name.
audit.why: Every spike in this entry is written as a mood rather than a timing. 'Do not offer him free windows' cannot be executed; 'step up only when The Darkin Glaive and Aureate Rush are both down, 10 seconds each' can. The numbers also change the shape of the advice: Grim Deliverance is 110/95/80, so his ultimate is a once-per-fight commitment you can bait, while Dreaded Return at 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 is the tool that actually catches a Sejuani trying to disengage.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive 10/9/8/7/6s, Dreaded Return 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, Grim Deliverance 110/95/80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cultivation of War lets Zaahen revive once he is filled with Determination, and he builds Determination from attacks and abilities against champions. Neither layer mentions it.
audit.why: It is the single fact that changes how a Sejuani plays every fight against him and it is completely absent. The entry's plan is 'start every fight with your R lockdown, and chain Permafrost through his frontline dive' — which is right, but it assumes killing him once ends the problem. It does not, and the stacks that arm the revive come from him hitting you, so a lane spent conceding repeated trades is a lane spent charging it. Committing the 120-second Glacial Prison on a Zaahen who is about to stand back up is the worst possible use of it.
audit.corrected: Cultivation of War stacks Determination off his attacks and abilities on champions, and at full it grants bonus attack damage and lets him revive — check the stacks before you spend Glacial Prison on him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (Cultivation of War: 'grant him stacks of Determination ... When filled with Determination, Zaahen gains increased Attack Damage and can revive')

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate interactions are absent: The Darkin Glaive is an auto-attack reset whose recast knocks up, Aureate Rush deals damage based on a percentage of health, and both The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance heal him.
audit.why: Each one contradicts a piece of advice the entry gives. The reset means the tell is the attack wind-up, not a cast animation, so a player watching for a spell steps back a beat late every time — and the recast knock-up is his only displacement, which is what actually breaks a Permafrost chain. The percent-health scaling means the entry's implicit 'stack tank stats and survive' plan is the wrong axis; armour does not answer it. And the double heal source means Grievous Wounds is a real item decision here, which neither layer mentions once.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive is an auto-reset and its recast knocks you up — watch the wind-up, not the cast. Aureate Rush scales off health, so armour reads it wrong, and both his Q and his R heal him: buy Grievous Wounds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (The Darkin Glaive: autoReset, knockup, heal; Aureate Rush: percentHealth; Grim Deliverance: heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in Zaahen's kit blocks projectiles, grants a spell shield, or provides untargetability. Glacial Prison lands on him unconditionally, and neither layer says so.
audit.why: The entry calls Sejuani's R her 'one real equaliser' but never explains what makes it reliable here specifically. Against most of the champions in this lane pool the R has to be scheduled around a wall, a pool or a stealth. Against Zaahen there is nothing to schedule around — the only thing that can stop the 1300-unit projectile is a body standing in front of him, because it stuns the first champion it hits. That is worth stating as the positive it is.
audit.corrected: He has no projectile block, no spell shield and no untargetability — Glacial Prison always lands. The only thing that stops it is another champion standing in front of him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json (no blocksProjectiles, spellShield or untargetable flags)

notes: The packet's flagged defect was right and total: not one of Zaahen's five abilities is named anywhere in either layer, and the full layer's matchup-defining cooldown is literally written as 'Zaahen Ultimate'. Best find: Cultivation of War lets him revive once he is filled with Determination, which he builds by hitting champions. The entry's plan is to concede repeated lane trades and then open every teamfight with Glacial Prison — that plan both charges his revive and risks spending a 120-second ultimate on a champion who is about to stand back up. Checking his stacks before committing R is the single highest-value habit in this matchup and it appears nowhere. Second: Aureate Rush deals damage as a percentage of health, so the entry's implicit 'be a tank and survive' axis is the wrong one, and both The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance heal him, making Grievous Wounds a real buy that neither layer mentions. Third: The Darkin Glaive is an auto-attack reset and its recast is what knocks you up — the tell is the attack wind-up, not a cast animation, and that knock-up is the thing that actually breaks a Permafrost chain. Fourth, and a positive worth stating: nothing in his kit blocks projectiles, spell-shields, or goes untargetable, so Glacial Prison lands unconditionally — the only thing that stops it is a teammate's body, because it stuns the first champion hit.
